title: Grateful Dead Live at The Music Box on 1969-02-04
lineage: SBD > CM > C > D > CD > EAC > shntool > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: Fuzzy soundboard recording of a smoking ’69 show with standout Dark Star/St. Stephen/Eleven sequence and killer Other One → Alligator → Caution, but noticeable tape hiss and drum loss.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – school‑girl opens the set, followed by scorching Morning Dew, a tight Dark Star into St. Stephen and Eleven, and an inspired second‑set climax with The Other One, Alligator and one of the best Caution jams of the era. Recording quality is mixed: the SBD tape has noticeable hiss, a fast‑running speed that shifts pitch, muddy mids and drums often buried, plus occasional cuts, yet most listeners find it listenable enough to enjoy the music.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality consistently receives 4‑5‑star praise with many standout moments; recording quality is described as marginal/fuzzy, lowering the overall score but not enough to outweigh the strong performance.

recording_quality.technical_notes: General muddiness and tape hiss from cassette generation; drums often lost in mix; tape runs fast (key shift on Dark Star); occasional cuts (Schoolgirl intro, end of Feedback) but overall the mix remains balanced enough for listening.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set builds nicely with a raunchy GMLSG and strong early jams; the Dark Star → St. Stephen → Eleven sequence drives momentum into a superb second set where The Other One segues into Alligator and then an intense Caution jam, ending with a wild Feedback finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is highlighted – dynamic playing on Dark Star, beautiful tone on Morning Dew, strong lead into the Alligator/Caution transition, and even a shouted “Alligator” cue.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ is noted as deep and present despite overall muddiness; keyboards sit well in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Drum presence is uneven – some reviewers hear drums almost lost, while others praise Bill and Mickey’s energy throughout the show.
